cards.text: All the people pack together into the square before the Water Gate. And no, friend, they're not there to complain about traffic. They've got a request for Ezra the scribe.

cards.question: The whole crowd in the square asks Ezra the scribe to bring something out to them. What is it?

answers.text: The Book of the Law of Moses

cards.text: So on the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brings the Law out before the assembly. Men, women, and all who can listen and understand.

cards.question: Ezra faces the square and reads the Law aloud to the crowd. How long does he keep reading?
During Ezra's long reading, the crowd stops paying attention to the Book of the Law.

cards.text: Ezra's up on a high wooden platform built for this occasion, with six men on his right and seven on his left. Thirteen men backing him up. Back in the junk drawer, my backup was a twist tie.

cards.question: Ezra opens the book in full view of everyone, since he's standing above them all. What do the people do as he opens it?

cards.text: Then Ezra blesses the LORD, the great God. Hands go up all over the square, and the people say, “Amen, Amen!”

cards.question: After the people answer Ezra's blessing with Amen, how do they worship the LORD?

answers.text: Bowing with faces to the ground
Dancing and singing in the square

cards.text: Then a team of thirteen Levites goes to work, teaching the people the Law as they all stand in their places.

cards.question: As the Book of the Law is read in the square, what's added so the people can understand what they're hearing?
As the people in the square hear the words of the Law, what does the whole crowd start doing?

cards.text: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites tell everyone, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep.”

cards.question: Nehemiah tells the weeping crowd to go home and go without food for the rest of the holy day.

cards.text: NOPE. Nehemiah tells them to go eat what's rich and drink what's sweet. A holy day that comes with a FEAST? Somebody write that down and put it on the fridge.

cards.question: Nehemiah also tells the people to send out portions from their feast. Who are the portions for?
Nehemiah tells the people not to grieve on this holy day. What does he say is their strength?

cards.text: The Levites go through the crowd calming everybody down: “Be still, since today is holy. Do not grieve.”

cards.question: Then all the people eat, drink, send out portions and rejoice greatly. Why?

answers.text: They understood the words made known to them
The work on the wall was finally done
Their enemies had finally given up

cards.text: Next day, the second day of the month, a group gathers around Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law. Day one, they listened for HOURS. Day two, they're BACK. Nobody hit snooze.

cards.question: On the second day of the month, who gathers around Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law?

answers.text: Family heads plus priests and Levites
The governor and the city guards

cards.question: Studying the Law, they find what the LORD commanded through Moses for the feast of the seventh month. Where were the Israelites to dwell during the feast?

cards.text: The Law also says to proclaim this and spread it through their towns and in Jerusalem. The message starts with a trip out to the hill country.

cards.question: To make the booths, what does the message tell people to bring back from the hill country?

cards.text: Olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm and other leafy trees. A whole orchard about to become somebody's walls.

cards.question: Once they have the branches, the people build booths only inside the courts of the house of God.

cards.text: Booths go up on rooftops, in courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, and in the squares by the Water Gate and by the Gate of Ephraim. You can't take ten steps without walking into somebody's living room!
The whole assembly that came back from exile makes booths and lives in them.

cards.question: The Israelites who returned from exile are living in booths for the feast. How long has it been since Israel celebrated like this?

cards.text: And there was great rejoicing. Nothing like this since JOSHUA, and here I thought my years in the junk drawer felt long!

cards.question: While the people live in booths for the feast, how often does Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God?
The Israelites keep the feast for ___ days, and on the ___ day they hold an assembly, according to the ordinance.

cards.text: That's where we'll leave it for now, friend. The Word's been read, and trust me, Nehemiah's story is far from done.

findings.problem: The passage opens mid-story ('At that time') as passage 8 of 13 in the Nehemiah group. The opening card never says where this is (Jerusalem) or who these people are (the Israelites back from exile, now settled in their towns). It spends one of its three sentences on a traffic joke instead. The joke also doesn't click: a crowd gathering to hear the Law has little in common with complaining about traffic.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Ezra's up on a high wooden platform...', 'Thirteen men backing him up.' and 'Back in the junk drawer, my backup was a twist tie.' Only the opening card may have 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: 'NOPE.', 'Nehemiah tells them...', 'A holy day that comes with a FEAST?' and 'Somebody write that down and put it on the fridge.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'NOPE.' right after the true or false on card 14. Every baker sees this card, whatever they picked, so it reads as a verdict on the baker's answer. To a baker who answered True, it reads as being told they were wrong. To a baker who answered False, it doesn't make sense. Answer reactions belong in answer-explanations.md, not on a story card.

rule.text: Never says "wrong," "fail" or "bad" about a baker's answer. The reaction phrases for right and missed answers are in answer-explanations.md.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates this stop by a wide margin: 9 multiple choice, 2 true or false, 0 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates this stop too: 5 multiple choice, 1 true or false, 1 fill in the blank. Both stops follow the same pattern, heavy on multiple choice with a single true or false.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: 'Next day... to study the words of the Law.', 'Day one, they listened for HOURS.', 'Day two, they're BACK.' and 'Nobody hit snooze.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards are discovery questions that can't be reasoned out from earlier cards. Card 2 asks who gathers on day two, card 3 asks where they dwell during the feast, card 10 asks since whose days, and card 13 asks for the number of feast days and the day of the assembly. Only cards 5, 7 and 12 are informed guesses.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Joshua son of Nun shows up for the first time here, as the right answer, and again on card 11 as 'JOSHUA'. He is never introduced. This matters more here because a Levite named Jeshua was named in verse 7.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: A baker could argue for the wrong answer 'Since the days of Solomon'. Solomon kept the feast for seven days with an assembly on the eighth day (2 Chronicles 7:8-9), which is the same shape as this celebration.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank is verse 18's wording with two numbers removed (seven, eighth). No earlier card gives the baker anything to reason from. Grammar also sorts the words: only 'seven' and 'three' fit 'for ___ days'. So the card tests unseen wording and luck, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The closing line is nearly a copy of the doc's example: 'That's where we'll leave it for now, friend... trust me... far from done' against the example 'And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
